name: Trace Waterfall
summary: A tracing-UI film: log stream, then cascading spans where one coral span after deploy #2231 explains the −18%.
look: Near-black observability UI, mono type throughout, teal span bars cascading down a time ruler with hairline guides. One long coral span and a teal-outlined Pulse card carry the anomaly.

components.name: Log line
components.role: mono timestamp + level + service + message, 20 px

components.name: Span bar
components.role: rounded bar on a time ruler, indented by depth

components.name: Time ruler
components.role: top tick labels with hairline guides down the frame

components.name: Hot span
components.role: coral span + lighter child for the deploy that caused it

components.name: Pulse card
components.role: teal-outlined panel with the anomaly and the two actions

components.name: Resolved span
components.role: green bar that closes the incident

motion.name: Log scroll
motion.how: text rows translate −38 px every 0.25 s (8th notes at 120 BPM) with steps(1) for a terminal feel

motion.name: Span cascade
motion.how: each span scaleX 0 → 1 from its start with power3.out 0.3 s, children staggered 0.125 s (16ths)

motion.name: Hot-span overrun
motion.how: coral span keeps growing linearly past the ruler guide over 2 beats, then card y +60 → 0 back.out(1.4) 0.4 s on the snare

story: Hook: a log stream scrolls past with a WARN nobody reads. Drop: acme.pulse watch() is the root span over every metric. Proof: a checkout trace with payment.authorize running long in coral after deploy #2231, Pulse card with −18% since 09:42, Roll back. CTA: one green resolved span, 6 min, Start free.
adapt: Use your own product's run logs or job steps as spans (pipeline stages, API calls, agent steps); the root span is your product watching, the anomaly is the one step that runs long.

references.note: flame graph conventions: width = time, depth = stack
what traces and spans are (parent/child units of work)

fit.risk: Engineers love it, buyers outside engineering may not; keep span names short and the −18% card dominant.
